transcript.text: Samsung WW90T534DAW keeps coming up with 4C after a couple of minutes. Drum is dry. Any ideas before I call someone out?

The 4C code on Samsung washing machines typically means there is a problem getting water into the drum within the first few minutes of starting a cycle. 1. Ensure the tap behind the machine is turned fully on.
2. Check if the inlet hose is kinked or squashed against the wall. If those are fine, the most likely culprit is a blocked mesh filter inside the water inlet port on the back of the machine. Please switch off and isolate the machine. Unscrew the fill hose from the back (have a towel ready for any residual water). Look into the small mesh filter inside the inlet port on the machine. Is it blocked with grit or scale, or does it look clean?
Tap was open, hose isn't kinked. I've taken the hose off and the mesh filter is clogged with grey grit and limescale bits.

That explains the 4C code perfectly—the grit and limescale were restricting the flow so much that the machine timed out waiting for water. If it still shows 4C after cleaning the filter, the next most likely cause is the water inlet valve itself (the solenoid that opens to let water in) failing or sticking. If you find it's not filling even with a clean filter and open tap, that would point to the valve needing replacement.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the fill-hose mesh filter is" — A small mesh filter sits inside the fill-hose connector at the tap/valve end and catches grit. Turn the tap off, unscrew the hose and rinse the mesh. Typical layout — your machine may differ.]
